findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews overdue notice counts on the first of every month. Historical figures are archived for five years before being summarized and retired."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph, or if it is meant to support the recommendation, explain how it relates to the return-rate or revenue analysis.
findings.violation: This detail about notice-count review and archival schedule is never connected to the pilot findings or the recommendation; it adds administrative trivia with no bearing on the argument.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews self-checkout usage at the end of each quarter. Branch-level totals roll up into the consortium's shared reporting dashboard."
findings.fix: Delete this paragraph or replace it with circulation data actually relevant to the fines decision.
findings.violation: Self-checkout usage has no stated relationship to overdue fines, return rates, or the pilot, making this a non-sequitur under a heading that should establish relevant background.

findings.evidence: "the on-time-or-eventual return rate for borrowed items held at 93 percent, compared with 86 percent at the branches that kept fines in place"
findings.fix: Report sample sizes and significance testing, and state how pilot branches were selected relative to non-pilot branches.
findings.violation: The comparison gives no sample sizes, confidence interval, or statistical test, and doesn't address whether the 5 pilot branches were selected randomly or differed systematically from the 5 comparison branches, so the 93%-vs-86% gap could reflect selection bias rather than the fine policy.

findings.evidence: "before the pilot to 5 percent after it... The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Either administer/report a survey at the 18-month mark or explicitly note why the 12-month reading is used and whether results held through month 18.
findings.violation: The pilot is described as 18 months long, but the "after" survey was taken at 12 months, so the survey doesn't actually cover the full pilot period being used to justify the recommendation.

findings.evidence: "self-reported avoidance of the library due to fear of fines dropped from 22 percent... to 5 percent after it"
findings.fix: Report the same survey administered at non-pilot branches over the same period, or note the absence of a control and qualify the causal claim accordingly.
findings.violation: The survey was only run at pilot branches with no comparison to non-pilot branches over the same period, so the drop cannot be distinguished from a general trend unrelated to fine elimination.

findings.evidence: "eliminates overdue fines for all item types at all ten branches"
findings.fix: Either present item-type-level pilot data or scope the recommendation to the item types actually tested.
findings.violation: Neither the pilot description nor any other part of the document indicates the pilot results were broken down by item type, so extending the finding to "all item types" is an unsupported generalization.

findings.evidence: "matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Either cite the actual pilot data showing a 60-day return pattern, or remove the claim that this threshold comes from the pilot.
findings.violation: No earlier part of the document states that the pilot measured a 60-day return window; the claim attributes a specific figure to the pilot data that was never reported, which is an unsupported (and seemingly fabricated) evidentiary claim.

findings.evidence: "The systems team plans to update the online catalog's fine-display field during the same rollout window."
